args.title: Reject non-integer TTL env values instead of silently truncating them
args.body:
File: src/config.ts

The `int()` helper used to parse `TOKEN_TTL_MINUTES` and `RESET_TOKEN_TTL_MINUTES` (and other numeric env vars) uses `Number.parseInt`, which happily parses a value like "12h" as 12 instead of rejecting it. This lets a misconfigured instance start up with a token lifetime of a few minutes instead of the intended 720. Change `int()` to only accept strings that are entirely digits (optionally signed), and throw the existing "must be an integer" error for anything else, including trailing unit suffixes.

args.title: Add a name filter to the reports list endpoint
args.body:
File: src/api/reports.ts

`GET /reports` only supports `page` and `pageSize`, so finding one report among hundreds means paging through the whole list. Add an optional `name` query parameter to this handler (passed through to `reportRepo.list`, likely as a case-insensitive substring match) so the reports page can offer a search box.

args.title: Document the password validation rules in the API reference
args.body:
File: docs/API.md

The reference describes `POST /auth/password-reset/confirm` as taking `{ token, password }` without saying what makes a password valid. The code (src/api/auth.ts) enforces `z.string().min(10).max(200)`; add a line noting the 10-200 character requirement so support staff don't have to find it by trial and error.

args.title: Honor q-weights when picking a locale from Accept-Language
args.body:
File: src/i18n/index.ts

`pickLocale` iterates the Accept-Language header's entries in the order they were written and returns the first one it supports, ignoring each entry's `;q=` weight. A header like "en;q=0.3, fr-FR;q=0.9" therefore resolves to English even though French is preferred. Parse each entry's q value (defaulting to 1 when absent), sort by weight descending, and return the first supported locale in that order.

This comment was written by RepoMind, an automated triage agent. To reach a person, mention @ledgerline/maintainers.

The `int()` helper in src/config.ts parses env vars with `Number.parseInt`, which reads "12h" as 12 instead of rejecting it, so a mistyped TTL is silently accepted as minutes. It should validate that the whole string is an integer and throw at startup otherwise, as priya-s suggested. Opened a draft PR proposing that fix.

This comment was written by RepoMind, an automated triage agent. To reach a person, mention @ledgerline/maintainers.

This matches the documented behaviour in docs/API.md: `/health` returns 503 only when the database is down, by design. A degraded queue is intentionally still reported with HTTP 200 (see src/api/health.ts) so the instance stays in rotation while work backs up rather than being pulled entirely. For the load balancer probe, treat 200 as "keep in rotation"; for alerting, watch the `status`/`checks.queue` fields in the JSON body separately rather than the HTTP status code.
